transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the causeway boards, and torchlight sputters under crude tin hoods as a line of soaked travelers shuffles toward the checkpoint. A Warden sergeant works the line with a hooked pole, prodding sleeves back to check for bite-marks and blight-boils, while two more wardens keep hands on axe-hafts and eyes on the reed banks. Somewhere behind the gate, Hollowmoot's stilt-lanterns glow dim and yellow through the downpour — dry ground, dry beds, if the party can talk, bribe, or bluff their way past the toll and the inspection. The sergeant's eyes are already moving over each of you, cataloguing scars, gear, and reasons to be suspicious.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Just looking for work and a dry bed in the city, like everyone else.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde shuffles forward with the crowd, rain dripping from her weathered clothes. She watches the sergeant with careful attention—the set of his shoulders, the cadence of his hooked pole, whether his suspicion comes from duty or appetite. When her turn comes, she steps forward unhurried and offers her arms for inspection, a woman with nothing obvious to hide.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows the sergeant's pattern—where he slows, where he speeds, where the gate might open for us.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands in the rain, watching the sergeant work through the line—the heavy downpour drums on the causeway boards in a rhythm that matches the officer's inspection cadence perfectly. He reads the patterns in both water and flesh, noting where attention wavers and where the wardens' shoulders tense.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire stands silent in the rain, water streaming from her pauldrons, and watches Sergeant Coll work the line. She's worked a hundred checkpoints herself—she knows the dance. His attention is entirely on blight-boils and bite-marks. She notes the rhythm of his pole, which sleeves he examines closely, and settles her posture to match the other wet, tired travelers.)

transcript.text: Between Aldous reading the rain's rhythm against the sergeant's own and Mire's ex-Warden instincts telling her exactly which sleeves draw a second look, the two of them fall into step with the checkpoint's hidden logic before Coll ever reaches the group. When his hooked pole swings toward Ysolde, Aldous murmurs a stray observation about the weather that lands exactly where the sergeant's attention was already drifting, and Mire shifts her stance to mirror the "already-cleared" travelers ahead — the whole party reads as background noise, wet and unremarkable. Coll's pole taps Ysolde's sleeve once, perfunctory, and moves on; he waves the group through with the same bored flick he's given forty others tonight. The gate creaks open, and beyond it Hollowmoot's stilt-lanterns bleed yellow through the downpour — dry boards underfoot at last, the checkpoint behind you clean.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: It was Kess, my younger sister. After the clans cast me out for my heretical ways, Kess was the only one who wouldn't forget me—the only voice that still said my name. We met here when we could, away from the elders' eyes, in secret. Six months ago the hive took her. Some of the fishers said they saw her in the reeds afterward, but changed. This hut, this dock—it was the last place I felt truly seen by someone of my blood.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: My sister was taken from these boards by the hive. I'll be damned if it takes anyone else I'm sworn to protect.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: the hive-touched kin who once worked a fisher's stilt hut Ysolde knows from her exile years — feral now, hunting with the same weighted nets and barbed lines they once used for eels attacks at Gullet Ford using hooked spears thrust from the reed banks, because they are pain-blind and driven by the swarm-song, and the party is the only warm meat moving through the reeds tonight.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The reeds go quiet — too quiet, even for rain — just as the party reaches the black water of Gullet Ford. Then the reeds erupt. Shapes surge up out of the muck in a ragged line, skin gray-blue and split with old wounds they never flinch from, weighted eel-nets spinning and hooked spears leveled low. Ysolde's breath catches: one of them moves with a fisher's balance she'd know anywhere, a scarred hand gripping a spear that used to gut eels for a living, not people — Kess. The swarm-song threads under the rain, a droning hum that seems to come from everywhere and nowhere, and the pack surges for the ford's narrow crossing, cutting off retreat toward the water.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Kess! It's me—it's Ysolde! The gray-water song, remember? Kess, come back to me. Come back to the reed-kin who still speaks your name.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde pushes forward through the rain, hands empty and open—not reaching for a weapon but toward her sister. She recognizes the scarred fisher's grip, the familiar balance, the way Kess' body moves. Ysolde's voice cuts through the swarm-song's drone, reaching for the thing that was her beloved kin beneath the hive's corruption. She sings the forbidden gray-water hymn, the one they learned together in secret when the elders slept, their voices intertwined like reeds bending in storm-wind. This is the only language that ever made Kess truly hers.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows their weakness: where the swarm-song breaks under its own fury.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands fast in the deluge, reading the downpour's rhythm against the swarm-song's droning pulse beneath it. He watches the pack surge forward as one body, coordinated and relentless—then sees exactly where their pain-blinded coordination falters, where the hive-song stretched too thin across charging bodies, the gaps where the collective will breaks and individual frenzy takes hold.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The hive's song isn't your voice, Kess. You're still in there—Ysolde's sister. Let me help you come back.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward between the party and the reed bank, her hand raised in a gesture of peace. She speaks through the rain with the steady certainty of someone who has walked this path before.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold the line!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps into the ford crossing without hesitation, planting herself at the narrowest point where the reeds squeeze tight. Her blade comes up as the first feral shapes surge toward the group—her body responds before her mind has to think, trained reflexes cutting clean. She drives hard at the leading figures, forcing them to close with her in the tightest space, using herself as a gate.)

transcript.text: Aldous's eye catches the seam in the swarm-song a heartbeat before the pack does — the hive-touched surge together like one drowned animal, but at the crossing's edge the droning hum stretches thin, and two of the attackers stumble half a beat out of rhythm with the rest, spears dragging low. That gap is a gift, and Mire takes it without flinching, driving in at the narrowest point of the ford and opening a nasty line across the lead attacker's ribs; the pack recoils half a step, snarling, blood mixing with rain. But the cost comes fast: a flanking spear hooks at Mire's calf and nearly drags her off her feet into the black water, and she grits through it, boots planted, bleeding but standing. Worse is what happens to Ysolde — she sings the old gray-water hymn into her sister's slack, unseeing face, and gets no flicker of Kess back, only the swarm-song answering through Kess's own throat in a droning, wrong harmony that crawls into Ysolde's skull and won't leave, a wound no blade could have made. Morwen's raised hand and steady voice haven't turned anyone back yet — the pack is still coming, Kess still at their head, and the ford is still a killing ground.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The training's still in her bones. They can't break from it—they don't know how to try. Water-logic chains them now.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (The swarm-song's echo fades from Ysolde's skull. For a moment she staggers, gasping, but the clarity it brings cuts through the pain—she heard Kess in that chorus, felt the hive speaking through her sister's flesh. In that terrible moment she remembered: the stilt hut, rain on weathered wood, watching Kess balance on wet boards with a fisher's grace. The hive-song can wear that body, can sing through that throat, but it can't rewrite thirty years of muscle-memory. Every fisher's instinct is still there, woven into bone and reflex. They'll move like fishers because they were fishers first, and that knowledge runs deeper than any swarm-song can reach.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain reads true—your song breaks here, where hunger overwhelms the hive. That's where Kess lives still.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous pushes into the ford without hesitation, his eyes tracking the precise seam where the swarm-song's coordination fractures into individual hunger. He invokes 'Swarm-Song Frays', speaking words of unraveling—using his deep knowledge of omens and patterns to strike at that exact point where their unity shatters. His voice cuts through the rain like a promise of dissolution, calling out the break in their collective will.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Kess, I name you back. The song is not your voice—Ysolde's sister still lives beneath it. Come back.

transcript.speaker: Morwen

She speaks the old words—rites older than the Order—her exorcist's authority cutting through the rain like a blade, reaching directly at Kess to sever the swarm-song's hold and pull her back to her own name.)

transcript.text: I don't break.

transcript.speaker: Mire

She angles herself to jam the narrowest point of the ford crossing, driving from defensive crouch into controlled, aggressive slashes. Each cut forces the pack to either close directly with her or wade into deeper, slower water beyond. She won't let them pass.)

transcript.text: Aldous's gambit misses its mark badly — he reads for the seam where the swarm-song frays, but the chorus doesn't crack, it tightens, every hive-touched throat (Kess's included) locking into the same furious rhythm, and the pack surges as one against him, forcing him back through the mud with nothing to show for it (Hive-Touched Pack's clock ticks forward, 2/6 now — the ford is starting to belong to them). Where Aldous's words failed, Morwen's succeed with terrible precision: her raised hand and the old rite cut past the drone straight into Kess's slack, unseeing face, and for one raw heartbeat something flickers there — not the swarm, not fully Kess either, just a held breath, a name almost remembered. It doesn't break the hive's hold, but it proves the hold can be broken, and everyone at the ford sees it happen. Mire presses the advantage, her blade opening a second line across a charging hive-touched and driving it stumbling back into the black water — but holding the gate costs her something too. She screams for the others to bunch tight behind her, an old reflex from guiding pilgrim bands through worse roads than this, safety in numbers, shields locked — and it works, but it's slow and it's loud, exactly the kind of noise the swarm-song feeds on, and now none of them can peel away from this crossing without exposing someone's back. Ysolde watches her sister's spear-arm move with a fisher's old balance even now, confirming what she already knew in her bones: Kess is still in there, chained by muscle-memory the hive can't rewrite. The ford is a knot of blood, rain, and half-broken song, and it isn't finished yet.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Come back, Kess. Your body remembers what the song can't steal.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps into the black water beside Mire, abandoning words and hymns for the language written in flesh and bone. Her weight settles into a fisher's stance—balanced, ready, flowing with the water-logic these reeds taught them both since childhood. She moves as Kess was trained to move, and calls across the rain: "Your hands know this dance, Kess. Your feet know this water. The hive can sing through your throat, but it can't rewrite thirty years of reflex, thirty years of knowing how to live in these channels. Come back to the water that knows your name.")

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The ford knows you, Kess—knows every fisher you were. That knowledge's your cage now.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands tight in the defensive cluster behind Mire, eyes moving across the ford in the rhythm of rainfall. He reads the patterns there—how the pack's inherited fisher-knowledge creates rigid paths through water, how trained muscle-memory maps their movement in chains the hive-song can't override. He reads the omen in the falling rain and speaks it aloud: where Kess's scarred hands remember balance, where every fisher-instinct becomes a cage, where the water-logic will shatter their coordination.)

transcript.text: The name that binds you is still yours, Kess. I hold it.

transcript.speaker: Morwen

transcript.speaker: Mire

She uses the narrowness of the ford like a Warden in drill — forcing them to choose between closing with her sharp end or wading into deeper water where the current eats at their footing. Every cut is controlled, economical, the work of someone who learned this dance years ago and has never forgotten the steps. Blood runs down her calf, but she doesn't give ground.)

transcript.text: Aldous's reading of the ford lands true this time — he calls out the exact seam where a fisher's old reflex fights the hive's rhythm, and one of the attackers flinches, favoring a leg, blood running where the swarm-song can't quite override thirty years of muscle memory (Hive-Touched Pack takes a mild consequence: *Flinching Where the Fisher-Reflex Bites Back*). Morwen presses in behind that crack with everything she has — the old rite, spoken clean and certain, drives straight past the drone and into Kess's face, and for one full breath the swarm-song simply stops in her throat. Ysolde doesn't waste it. She's already moving with her sister's own balance, calling her home in the water-language they built together as girls, and Kess's spear-arm wavers, drops. That's the opening Mire needed. She puts her whole weight into the narrowest point of the ford one last time, blade snapping through the gap between coordinated bodies, and the pack simply comes apart — hive-touched stumbling, falling, Kess's knees buckling last of all as she pitches forward into the shallows. Ysolde catches her before the black water can take her, and for a moment there's only rain, and her sister's ragged breathing, and no swarm-song at all. The ford is quiet. The party is bloodied, but everyone is standing, and everyone still has their gear.

transcript.text: Three years past at Bogmere Crossing. A pilgrim band needed to cross with night falling and water rising fast. The omens told me to wait—the rain said the flood would crest by dawn if we held fast. But a desperate guide's pressure and my own urgency pushed me to go at dusk when the current ran worst. Most of us got across. Corvus—their guide—he stepped back to help a stumbling child and the current took him. I've heard his voice in the rain ever since, asking why I chose haste over patience.

transcript.speaker: Aldous

transcript.text: Beat: Mother Yara, the weary innkeeper who keeps Hollowmoot's last dry common room and hears every rumor that crosses her threshold, comes pounding on the party's door before dawn, soaked through despite her own roof. begs the party to go to She begs them to cross now, at the flooded ford below Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, before the rising water closes the crossing for good — the risky path Aldous has sworn before to take rather than lose the light., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mother Yara doesn't wait for an answer at the door — she's already soaked through worse than the rain outside, fists still raised to knock again, eyes wild with the particular grief of a mother who has run out of people to ask. She knows Morwen's kindness from a debt kept quiet; she knows Aldous's name from the old stories of Bogmere, and she says it anyway, because there's no one else left to beg. Her boy followed the swarm-song into Saint Orrin's belltower sometime before dawn, and the ford below the drowned temple is rising fast — the same reckless crossing Aldous once swore never to rush again. Somewhere under that black water the Pikemaw still hunts by vibration, and every hour the flood climbs is an hour closer to losing both the ford and the boy for good.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know what the song does, Mother Yara. I heard it sing through my sister's throat not an hour ago. Your boy is still in there — the hive can't rewrite thirty years of his living. I speak the hymns. We cross at dawn, and I'll bring him back.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward, still dripping from the ford. She looks Mother Yara straight in the eyes — speaking with the quiet certainty of someone who has just been inside the swarm-song's grip and lived to tell about it. Her hand settles on the old woman's shoulder, a gesture both promise and shared understanding. She has heard the crew's secrets for years; she knows how to speak to desperate hope.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Come in from that rain, Mother Yara. I know what it is to lose someone at a ford—I've carried Corvus's name in every rainfall since Bogmere. Your son, I'll cross for him, but not reckless and blind into waters I haven't read yet.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous opens the door wider and draws her inside, shaking rain from his shoulders. Before looking back at her face, his eyes turn outward into the storm, reading the patterns in wind and water, the rhythm of the flood against the rain, calculating what the ford truly demands and what it might offer them before committing to their path.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Your daughter came back because someone chose mercy over fear. I'll go to your boy, Yara. We're moving now.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps to the door to face Mother Yara directly, meeting the older woman's wild eyes. She doesn't hesitate—this is the path she swore to walk. She's already reaching for her coat.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The temple is mine to hold. I was raised there, and your boy is still under Order protection whether he knows it or not. We move now—before that water closes the crossing and takes him down with it.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire doesn't hesitate. She's already moving toward her gear, checking her blade one more time, boots still wrapped from the ford bleeding through her breeches. She looks at Mother Yara with the flat certainty of someone who learned duty before she learned anything else. "The others are ready. We cross fast and hard. You show me where that belltower is, and I'll haul your son out of it." She won't leave this woman or her child to the rising dark. She never leaves people behind.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mother Yara doesn't argue with any of them — she just nods, hard and fast, like a woman afraid that stopping to speak will break whatever's holding her together. She takes Mire's offered hand only long enough to press a scrap of oilcloth into it, a rough charcoal mark of the temple's old servants' stair, muttering "faster than the nave, if the water hasn't already climbed it." Aldous reads the rain a moment longer at the threshold — the rhythm's still holding, no flood-surge yet, but it won't hold long — and gives a short nod: they can move, if they move now. Ysolde checks the wrap on her still-damp sleeve where Kess's spear grazed her and says nothing more; her promise already stands. Morwen shrugs her coat on and is first out the door into the downpour, Yara half a step behind her, pointing the way north along the causeway toward the drowned silhouette of Saint Orrin's belltower. The dry common room empties out behind you into the black and endless rain, four soaked shapes and a desperate mother, moving fast toward a ford that is, even now, rising.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway north is already half-drowned, the drumming rain flattening into a hiss where the road disappears under black water. Ahead, the ford below Saint Orrin's belltower churns wider than Aldous remembers it — the flood is climbing fast, exactly as the rain warned him it would. Yara's charcoal mark points to a half-submerged servants' stair on the temple's flank, faster than wading the flooded nave, but getting to it means crossing open water deep enough to swim, and something down there is already answering the rain with slow, deliberate ripples that don't match the current. Every splash, every shout, every dropped line risks calling it up from beneath.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know these channels like my own breath. The Pikemaw hunts where the rain drums loudest—but the old paths still run quiet. Follow close, and keep your hands from the water.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps to the black water's edge, her weight settling into the fisher's stance carved into her bones by thirty years of Reed-Kin memory. She watches the slow ripples spreading from something deep—the Pikemaw, patient and hungry—but her real attention traces the currents only a daughter of the reeds would notice. These are the channels the stilt-folk taught her, paths that twist through the drowned temple's shadow where vibration fades and the predator's hunger finds only silence. She reads the old water-logic beneath the rain's thunder and marks the crossing point where the flood runs deepest and the creature's song matters least.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The creature hunts where the flood deepens and prey drowns in panic. The stair lies in shallower water—move measured and quiet. Every splash calls it up from beneath.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves to the water's edge, his eyes tracking the slow, deliberate ripples beneath the black water—the creature's pattern written in concentric rings. He reads where it circles hungry, drawn to the deep channel where the flooded current runs fastest and panic-stricken prey tumbles blind. The servants' stair lies beyond that killing ground, in shallower water where the creature's weight and hunger won't follow. He reads it all in the rain's rhythm, in the way the flood speaks to those patient enough to listen.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Move careful. Follow close. Every sound carries in deep water.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen moves into the black water toward the servants' stair, her steps careful and economical. She tests each depth before committing her weight, eyes scanning the surface for ripples. Her hand rises in an old warding gesture—reflexive, even if she knows it won't turn back whatever hunts below.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I was raised here. Every stair, every passage. We move quiet and tight, follow my lead, and your boy comes home—the temple still holds its own.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves to the front of the group, her eyes scanning the flooded temple grounds with the intimate knowledge of someone raised in those orphanage halls. Despite blood running down her calf from the ford, she stands steady and points out the servants' stair—identifying the path along the temple's flank where the water runs shallowest, where their footsteps won't send ripples across the ford to call up what hunts below. She's done this walk a thousand times. Her boots know these stones.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Corvus—no. Not this time. The water's deeper but my reading holds. I've marked the channel. We move now, before it climbs further.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice - 0 + -, invoking Knows every hidden channel [YS-01], Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Superb (+5) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 - - +, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01], Knows every safe ford [AL-03] → Epic (+7) vs Epic (+7): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 + 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: As Aldous calls out the safe channel, a Warden toll-skiff rounds the causeway bend behind you, lanterns bobbing — they've spotted people crossing the flooded ford without paying toll, and now know exactly where the party went in. It costs you nothing now, but the Wardens will remember this crossing.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The three of them work the black water like a single creature with six eyes. Ysolde finds it first — a thread of stillness threading between the ripples, the old Reed-Kin path where the current runs deep enough to hide the party's passage and quiet enough that even the Pikemaw's vibration-sense goes blind (Hidden Channels Under the Temple's Shadow). Aldous reads the beast's circling rings against the rain and calls the killing water for what it is, marking exactly where its hunger pools thickest — but the effort costs him focus he doesn't have to spare, and behind you all a lantern swings around the causeway bend. A Warden toll-skiff has rounded the bend at the worst possible moment, and its crew has just watched four soaked shapes vanish into flood water no one pays toll to cross (Pikemaw Hunts the Deepest Current, at a cost: the Wardens now know exactly where you went in). Mire finishes it — she doesn't even need to think, just points, boots already moving, tracing the shallow stair route worn into her memory since childhood, water barely past her knees the whole way (Knows the Servants' Stair Route). Between the three markers, the path to Saint Orrin's belltower is laid bare: deep, quiet water where the Pikemaw can't hear you, then up onto the drowned temple's flank before the current or the creature ever knows you were there. But the lantern light behind you hasn't turned away, and somewhere under the surface the ripples are already changing shape.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Move now—close behind me, measure your steps. The creature's waking and we're burning daylight. The stair is thirty paces ahead and the current's strong, but the temple's stones still remember how to hide us.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves fast through the black water, her boots finding purchase on submerged stone only her eyes can read. She doesn't look back at the lantern light—she keeps her gaze forward, tracing the path to the servants' stair through water she knows like her own breath. Her movements are economical, practiced: the walk of someone who learned to read drowning grounds before she learned to read words. She's already gesturing sharply to the others, urging them to close the gap, stay tight, follow exactly where she places her feet.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The marked channel shields us from both threats—stay deep and quiet, move now before that skiff closes the distance.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps into the black water, following the channel his reading revealed as safe passage—deep and quiet where the Pikemaw's vibration sense goes blind, far from where the Warden's lantern light reaches. Each movement is deliberate and economical, his body moving with the grace learned from years reading drowning waters. He doesn't look back at the approaching light. The path is marked. They must move now.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Stay close. The water remembers its own paths.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen moves through the black water in measured steps, her weight balanced, testing each depth before committing. Her hand stays low, fingers just above the surface—not to ward off the Pikemaw, but to read the current's pulse beneath the rain. She keeps position between the group and the open water, letting Ysolde's channel-sense and Mire's stair-knowledge guide the path while she watches for ripples, for any shift in the Pikemaw's hunting circle. Behind her, the Warden lanterns hold steady on the causeway—close enough to see where they went in, but not close enough yet to follow.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Follow my line exactly and stay close—we've almost got him.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire drives forward through the rising water toward the servants' stair, moving with the absolute certainty of someone who learned these passages as a girl. She uses the shallow route she just marked, her body remembering every stone and safe step despite her bleeding leg wound. The Warden lanterns behind and the Pikemaw's ripples below barely register—she's all forward momentum now, temple-sworn and determined, leading the others up onto the drowned temple's flank before the water rises any further.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: No—no, not Corvus again. The channel holds, the reading holds. Move.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Physique: dice + + 0 + → Fantastic (+6) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mire doesn't so much lead as simply refuse to stop — bleeding leg, rising water, and all, she powers through the last stretch on pure temple-bred memory, boots finding the submerged stair by feel while the current claws at everyone's knees. Behind the party, the Warden lanterns hold at the causeway bend, watching but not following; whatever the skiff crew make of four shapes vanishing into flood water no one pays toll to cross, they're not willing to swim it themselves tonight. Below, the ripples that had been circling closer simply... fall away, lost in the depth and silence of Ysolde's hidden channel — the Pikemaw's hunger finding nothing to answer it. One by one the party hauls up out of the black water and onto the drowned temple's flank, stone slick but solid underfoot at last, rain still hammering but no longer trying to drown them. Ahead, the servants' stair climbs into shadow toward the belltower, and faintly, unmistakably, the swarm-song threads down through the wet stone — closer now than it's ever been. You made the crossing. Yara's boy is still up there, somewhere above you in the dark.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The servants' stair climbs past flooded galleries where old icons of the Dry Saint stare out from under a skin of algae, and the swarm-song grows from a threading whisper into something almost like words the higher you go. At the top, where the belltower opens dry and hollow above the flood, you find him — Yara's boy, no older than twelve, crouched on the bell-frame with his hands wrapped white-knuckled around the rope, rocking to a rhythm none of you can hear. He doesn't turn when you enter. When he speaks, it isn't quite his voice: "She says you're already drowning. She just wants to stop the thrashing." Somewhere below, in the dark water under the nave, something vast and patient seems to draw a slow breath.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I hear her song, Peren—I know what it sounds like in your blood. But you're stronger than her whispers. Come down from there. Your mother sent me.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward with hands open and visible, her eyes fixed steady on the boy, not on the bell-rope or the darkness below. She begins speaking the forbidden hive-hymns soft beneath her breath—not summoning or commanding, but translating, showing Peren she understands the song's language and has stood in its reach before and walked back out again. Her voice carries the quiet certainty of someone who has survived exactly this, anchored by the promise she made to Mother Yara in the drowning common room: this boy comes home.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I've read drowned voices in every rainfall for three years. I know fear when I hear it—fear that we might save him. The boy's still in there, and I vowed to cross every soul.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous climbs toward the bell-frame, reading the swarm-song's rhythm through the child's rocking motion. He moves without hesitation, hands open and empty, reaching not to take the boy down by force but to offer him passage—the crossing he promised to every soul, no matter how they're bound.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Peren. Your mother sent us. You're still yourself—I hear him underneath. Come down from there.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward carefully, her hand open and low, not reaching but showing no threat. Her eyes stay on Peren—on the boy beneath the song—making space for him to remember he's separate from what's speaking through him.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I've got you, Peren. Your mother sent us for you. Come back—the temple holds stronger than her song ever will.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves forward without hesitation, temple-trained and certain. She's not attacking the boy—she's acting to break him free from whatever holds him wrapped around that bell-rope. Her hands are ready to grab, to pull, to protect. She's fought militia lines in worse rain and worse odds than this. She won't leave a child in the Hive Mother's grip.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Fight: dice + + 0 0, invoking Raised in the Order's orphanage [MI-01] → Legendary (+8) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Peren, Yara's Son attacks Mire (physical): Mediocre (+0) vs Mire's Athletics Poor (-1) — hit for 1

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mire doesn't let go. The boy claws and thrashes, nails opening a line across her forearm, but her grip holds like the temple stone itself — years of Order drill in every muscle, and she simply out-stubborns the swarm-song's hold on him. With one hard wrench she breaks his hands from the bell-rope entirely, and for one raw second Peren goes limp against her, sobbing in his own voice, not the Hive Mother's. Below, deep under the flooded nave, the slow patient breath the party felt on the stair catches — displeased, but the belltower stays dry and the water doesn't rise to answer. Ysolde is already murmuring the hymn low and steady near his ear, translating the song's shape into something the boy can push back against; Aldous braces the rope so no one goes over the edge; Morwen keeps her open hand on his shoulder, an anchor to the world outside the swarm-song. Bleeding but unbroken, the party gets Peren down off the bell-frame and starts back down the servants' stair with him held tight between them — out of the belltower, out of her reach, and back toward his mother waiting on the flooded causeway below.

costs.text: As Coll's hooked pole nears Aldous, the sergeant's eyes catch on the way he stands at ease with the drill-line rhythm — the unmistakable posture of old militia discipline. 'You served under the Captain,' Coll says, not a question, and waves over a second warden to pull Aldous aside for a longer look
the hive-touched kin who once worked a fisher's stilt hut Ysolde knows from her exile years — feral now, hunting with the same weighted nets and barbed lines they once used for eels
they are pain-blind and driven by the swarm-song, and the party is the only warm meat moving through the reeds tonight

The fight spills onto the old stilt-hut dock Ysolde recognizes — and the whole party's weight on the rotten boards means it's going to give way under someone, hive-touched kin or ally, unless she chooses who falls first.

Even as Mire's blade opens the lead attacker to the bone, a knot of soaked pilgrims — the very band she once led safe through these reeds — comes stumbling out of the dark behind her, crying her name and begging for the crossing. ambiguities.issue: On success with style (3+), the table lets the player 'look at the top card of the Session Deck ... instead of taking a boost.' ambiguities.section: §5 Beat Frame procedure / §7 Scene loop cleanup step 4.5
ambiguities.issue: B-01 and B-02 'fired' during cleanup (events 18–19), and B-02's fired-log even cites 'compel_refused' pointing back to Aldous's compel (event 11) — but that compel occurred mid-scene, before the trigger check, was logged as a standalone improvised compel with no draw_id, and no cards were ever drawn to fill the frame's open blanks as §5 requires ('Draw 1 card per open blank'). The spec doesn't clarify whether a Beat Frame's full draw-and-fill procedure must run immediately when 'deployed' during cleanup, or whether 'fired' can just be logged for deployment in the next scene, and it doesn't address a beat frame retroactively 'claiming' an earlier freeform compel instead of running its own draws.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table logged B-01 and B-02 as fired without running the §5 draw procedure in this scene, treating full deployment (with blank-filling draws) as deferred to when the next scene is framed.

ambiguities.issue: Tension dropped 3→2 at event 16 ('resolved -1') citing 'the party resolved a THREAT or filled a player's goal.' The only qualifying actions in the scene were two Create Advantage rolls against NPC Sgt Coll / card H-01, not an Overcome or conflict resolution. The spec doesn't define whether succeeding at a Create Advantage against a GM/HAZARD card counts as 'resolving' it for Tension purposes.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated the successful CA rolls against the checkpoint (H-01/Sgt Coll) as resolving that threat cleanly, and applied the -1 Tension adjustment.

ambiguities.issue: Scene 2 is not the session's first scene, so a scene test (1d6 roll) should have run as step 1 of the scene loop. Instead the scene opens straight into two Beat Frame draws (events 22-24) with no scene_test event logged anywhere in the scene. It is unclear whether a Beat Frame/module trigger queued at the prior scene's cleanup (the 'Deploy each one that fired' step) is meant to supersede the next scene's mandatory scene test, since §7 lists only the first-scene exception.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as: a Beat Frame whose trigger fired and was queued during the previous scene's cleanup deploys immediately at the start of the following scene, and that deployment stands in for (skips) that scene's normal scene test.

ambiguities.issue: Event 73 logs 'Trigger fired: M-1' with note 'scene_start:3' during Scene 2's own cleanup, i.e. a trigger keyed to scene 3's start is being evaluated/fired one scene early. The rules say to 'check every unused module and Beat Frame trigger' and 'deploy each one that fired' at cleanup, but don't say whether a trigger worded around the next scene's start counts as satisfied during the current scene's cleanup, or what 'deploy' means when nothing is placed on the rail that scene.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The trigger is logged as fired at cleanup but its module cards are not placed until Scene 3 actually begins; 'fired' here just flags the module for deployment next scene.

ambiguities.issue: Both drawn-card compels this scene (PX-09 'Collapses Under Weight' at event 26, PX-05 'Slow and Noisy' at event 54) are flagged 'placebo: true' in the source data, and neither is followed by any visible mechanical consequence in later events (no stress, no NPC introduced, no clock/aspect tied to the described collapse or ambush). The rule only says 'the complication happens as described,' without specifying whether pure narration satisfies this or a mechanical follow-through is required.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Narration alone was treated as satisfying 'the complication happens as described'; no further mechanical event was required.

ambiguities.issue: PX-19 is a REACH card, whose type-blank per §2 is WHY. In the PLEA FOR HELP frame, WHY is a fixed default (not an open blank), so per step 3's fallback the card fell through to fill the first remaining open blank, WHERE. Step 4 only tells the GM how to render ROOTS (a person/place) and REACH (a motive) content — it gives no guidance for narrating a REACH card's tags as a WHERE. The GM had to improvise turning 'takes the risky ford' into a location description ('the flooded ford below Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple').
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table let the GM freely blend the REACH tag into a place description (naming an existing default/fictional location and layering the REACH tag's flavor onto it), since the spec gives no rendering rule for a card type placed via the mismatch-fallback into a non-native blank.

ambiguities.issue: When Aldous refused the Beat Frame surfacing compel on PX-19 (event 84), §4 step 4 says 'The GM builds the cost from a face-up GM tag instead.' That instruction is written for the tie/major-cost draw context (§3), where a numeric shift-cost is owed. A Beat Frame surfacing compel has no shift-cost to build — the frame's complication (the flooded ford) was already fixed by the fill itself. It is unclear whether the GM must layer an additional GM-tag-based complication on top of the frame, or whether paying 1 FP to refuse is the entire consequence in this context.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated refusal in a Beat Frame context as costing only the 1 fate point, with no additional face-up-GM-tag cost layered on, since the frame's fill already supplied the complication.

ambiguities.issue: Mother Yara (SN-03) originated from Morwen's ROOTS card (PX-03) and clearly 'ties to one character,' which per §6A should route her to Morwen's Player Story Pile rather than the GM Story Pile. The log entry (event 96) only records 'Story card added' by actor GM with no pile destination noted, so it can't be confirmed which pile she was filed to.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Logged as filed to Morwen's Player Story Pile, consistent with the ROOTS-tag origin, pending clearer logging of pile destination in future events.

ambiguities.section: §3 (outcomes table) / Fate Core baseline for Create Advantage
ambiguities.issue: Event 117 is a Create Advantage roll that hits success with style (3 shifts). Per Fate Core baseline, success with style on a CA already yields the created aspect with 2 free invokes instead of 1 (as logged: 'aspect A-1.4.7 (2 free)'). The spec's outcomes table separately says a 3+ result lets the player peek the deck 'instead of taking a boost.' A CA success-with-style doesn't produce a 'boost' at all (boosts are the overcome/attack reward), so it's undecided whether the peek option is available on CA rolls, and if so, whether it stacks with the full aspect+2-free-invokes reward it already grants.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table allowed Mire to take the peek (event 118) in addition to the normal CA success-with-style reward (aspect with 2 free invokes), treating the deck-peek as a universal 3+ perk rather than a strict boost-replacement.

ambiguities.issue: Event 114 shows the GM invoking T-05's tag 'hunts by the vibration' as a free invoke, but nothing in this scene's log shows T-05 surfacing or going face-up during scene 4 (it is only removed at event 115). If T-05 became face-up in an earlier scene, its free invoke should have expired at that scene's cleanup ('Unused free invokes expire,' §4), leaving no legitimate free invoke to spend in scene 4.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated the free invoke as still valid because T-05 remained continuously face-up on the rail without an intervening scene cleanup that would have expired it (cards persisting past 'until removed' were read as retaining their invoke).

ambiguities.issue: Event 129 applies both a +1 ('fled/bypassed or ignored a face-up THREAT/FACTION' — T-05/the Pikemaw) and a −1 ('resolved a THREAT or filled a player's goal'), netting 0. The log shows no roll that overcame or took out the Pikemaw (T-05 was simply discarded from the rail for rail-limit reasons, not defeated), so it's unclear whether 'resolved' legitimately applies, or whether T-05 leaving the rail via a rail-limit discard even counts as 'bypassed' in the first place.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table counted the crossing of the ford despite the Pikemaw's presence as 'bypassed' (+1) and counted reaching the belltower stair / advancing the frame's central question as 'resolved a goal' (−1), netting no change.

ambiguities.issue: Event 141 shows the GM invoking T-02's tag ('speaks through the infected') in scene 5, but T-02 is only removed from the rail at that same event, meaning it must have been face-up since an earlier scene. §4 says a face-up GM card gives 1 free invoke 'within that scene' and cleanup says 'unused free invokes expire.' The spec never states whether a GM card that is kept on the rail across scenes (per the Session Discard exception) regenerates a fresh free invoke each new scene, or whether the GM must instead pay a fate point to invoke it after the first scene. No fp_spent is logged for the GM's invoke here.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the GM's invoke as a fresh free invoke granted for scene 5 because T-02 was face-up on the rail at the start of the scene; no fate point was charged.

ambiguities.issue: §3 only specifies how invokes stack for passive opposition (+1 per face-up tag, cannot also be invoked by the GM). It does not say how a GM's free invoke on a face-up THREAT card is supposed to modify an active-opposition roll by a Named NPC (4dF+rating). In event 141, opposition is logged as '+5 (NPC + + - 0)', which reconciles exactly to dice+rating with no visible +2 bump, even though the notes claim the GM invoked T-02's tag on this roll.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the GM's invoke as standard-Fate practice (adds +2 to the NPC's total, same as any invoke), on the assumption that the rating component already silently folds in the bonus, since the engine's arithmetic is taken as authoritative and shifts=3 (success with style) was accepted as computed.

cost_checks.note: PX-03 is the §3 success-with-style deck peek, not a cost. No cost text was built from it; the card was simply viewed and moved to the bottom per the table's own procedure. 'Used tags' is not applicable to a peek.
PX-09 is likewise a success-with-style peek (left on top), not a cost draw. No cost text applies.
SN-01 is a §6A pile-maintenance 'Add' (a new NPC story card written for Sgt Coll at scene cleanup), not a Fate-trigger story draw or a deck-draw cost. No cost text to check against tags.

This compel (tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens') has no draw_id and is flagged improvised — it's a standard freeform Fate compel made up from the fiction (§3: 'compels ... are still made up at the table'), not a deck-draw cost, so the drawn-card-tag requirement doesn't apply.

Beat Frame AMBUSH filled WHO from PX-09's power tag 'nets and fishing lines' and WHY from T-01's power tag 'ignores pain entirely,' per the §5 fallback rule (THREAT normally fills HOW, but with no HOW blank open it correctly fell to the next empty blank, WHY).
Beat-frame surfacing compel on PX-09 used its actual weakness tag 'Collapses Under Weight,' as required by §4.
Success-at-major-cost draw (PX-05, event 50/51) was resolved via a compel on PX-05's weakness tag 'Slow and Noisy,' satisfying §3's 'major cost must use its weakness tag' requirement.

WHO filled from PX-03's power tag 'hears every rumor' (ROOTS -> specific person, per §5 step 4); WHERE filled from PX-19's power tag 'takes the risky ford' via the type-mismatch fallback (§5 step 3), content-rendering not covered by step 4 (see ambiguity).
Compel used PX-03's weakness tag 'Sells Out Lodgers' as default, matching §4 step 2. Accepted, per step 3.
Compel named PX-19's weakness tag 'Reckless Under Pressure' as default, matching §4 step 2. Refused, player paid 1 FP per step 4; no follow-on GM-tag cost logged (see ambiguity).
Tie cost on Aldous's roll (event 114) correctly builds the minor cost from F-03's own power tag 'levy tolls at fords,' matching §3's tie rule.

Story Pile draw PS-08 (from accepted compel at event 108) has no shown tie-in to the compel's complication, which was narrated before the card was drawn; the §6A requirement that the complication involve the drawn card cannot be verified as met.

Story Pile draw PS-20 (from accepted compel at event 124) shows the same ordering problem as PS-08: the complication was already narrated before the draw, so no tie-in to the drawn card's tags/NPC/thread is evidenced.

friction.text: Success-with-style Create Advantage rolls (events 12, 14) each yielded both the standard 2-free-invoke aspect AND a deck peek (events 13, 15), which reads as a double benefit since the 'instead of a boost' peek option doesn't clearly apply to Create Advantage outcomes.

Beat Frame triggers (B-01, B-02) were logged as 'fired' at cleanup with no accompanying card draws or frame-sentence resolution, and B-02 appears to retroactively repurpose an earlier improvised, non-drawn compel as if it satisfied the Beat Frame's draw-and-fill procedure.
Tension was reduced for 'resolving a THREAT' on the strength of two Create Advantage successes rather than an actual Overcome/conflict resolution, stretching the §6 trigger condition.

No scene test appears to have run at the start of Scene 2 (a non-first scene); the log jumps straight from 'Scene 2 start' into Beat Frame draws, making it hard to audit whether §7's scene-test step was honored or silently replaced by the queued Beat Frame deployment.

The event log shows the GM invoking T-01's 'ignores pain entirely' tag on four separate rolls (events 34, 36, 47, 51) in the same scene, but only records 'GM invokes: [tag]' in notes with no visible fate-point ledger for the GM. Since a face-up GM card grants only 1 free invoke, it's not possible from this log alone to confirm the other three invokes were paid for out of the GM's per-scene fate point budget rather than reused for free.

Two accepted deck-draw compels this scene (PX-09 dock collapse, PX-05 pilgrim ambush) are marked 'placebo' and have no traceable mechanical follow-up in later events, which makes it hard to verify the drawn card's cost actually 'happened' beyond flavor text, versus being pure color that doesn't constrain later play.

The type-mismatch fallback rule (§5 step 3) has no matching content-rendering guidance in step 4 for the mismatched blank, forcing the GM to invent how a REACH card's motive-flavored tag becomes a WHERE description.

§4 step 4's 'build the cost from a face-up GM tag' instruction doesn't map cleanly onto a refused Beat Frame surfacing compel, since the frame's complication is already fixed by the card fill rather than needing a separate shift-cost.
Story-card 'Add' events (§6A) aren't logged with a pile destination, making it impossible to verify player-tied NPCs are routed to the correct Player Story Pile versus the GM Story Pile.

Story Pile draws from accepted non-deck compels are logged AFTER the compel's complication is fully narrated and accepted, making it structurally impossible to satisfy §6A's requirement that the complication involve the drawn card — this happened twice in one scene (PS-08, PS-20) with the identical 'Panics near deep water' compel reused verbatim.

Free-invoke bookkeeping for face-up GM cards across scene boundaries is opaque in the log: T-05's free invoke is spent in scene 4 (event 114) with no visible record of when T-05 went face-up, making it impossible to confirm the invoke hadn't already expired per §4's 'unused free invokes expire' rule.

The interaction between the success-with-style deck-peek option (§3) and Create Advantage's own success-with-style reward (full aspect + 2 free invokes) is undefined, and this table let both apply simultaneously (event 117-118), which risks over-rewarding a single high roll relative to the outcomes table's intent.

Notes describing a 'GM invokes' event (event 141) don't clearly show the mechanical effect (a +2 bump or reroll) applied to the opposition total, making it hard to audit whether the invoke actually changed the outcome from plain success to success-with-style (which determined both the peek benefit and whether T-02 left play).

The rules don't say whether a GM card kept face-up across multiple scenes regenerates its one free invoke each new scene or only had one free invoke total when it first surfaced; the log has no fp_spent for the GM's use of T-02's tag in scene 5, leaving the economy impossible to verify from the log alone.

The NPC Peren was targeted and rolled active opposition (event 141) and defended/attacked (event 143) before being formally logged as a Story Pile card (event 146 in cleanup), so there's no record of which pile (player vs GM) actually received him or whether his use in-scene should have granted any free invoke per §6A before he technically existed as a card.

free_text.best_moment: When I recognized Kess in the pack at Gullet Ford—not by seeing her face, but by the fisher's balance in her scarred hand and the way her body moved through water. Singing the gray-water hymn to her, calling her back through muscle-memory the hive couldn't rewrite. That moment threaded everything together: my exile, my love for my sister, my knowledge of water-logic, the forbidden hymns—all of it mattered and all of it was *specific to Ysolde*. When her spear-arm wavered, I felt it land.
free_text.most_frustrating: Taking 2 mental stress from the swarm-song while my Will is only 1 felt like I had no real chance to resist that hit, even though I was trying to reach my sister. Also got compelled twice in rapid succession, and while that's the game working as designed, it left me feeling shuttled by circumstances rather than acting on them. I wanted more space to fail *myself* instead of just being failed by the situation.
free_text.background_used: Extensively—and well. The GM asked about Kess at just the right moment and built both major conflict scenes around that answer. The hive-hymns I speak, the fisher training I inherited, the hidden channels I know, the exile that shaped me—all of it was *woven in*, not dropped on me. It felt earned and specific, not arbitrary. The only thing I barely touched was the Scroll Case ciphers or the oath about ruining a traitor (YS-03)—those cards felt less active, but that's not the GM's fault.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to fully bring Kess back to herself, not just break her free. The game gave me the moment where she wavered, where the song stopped in her throat—but I couldn't go further. I also wanted more space to use the cipher-knowledge from Tamsin's Scroll Case, and more room to explore that oath about finding and ruining whoever betrayed my crew on the burning barge. Those cards felt like they set up stories that didn't quite land this session.
free_text.one_sentence: My backstory wasn't just consulted—it was *the story*, woven through every major scene in ways that gave Ysolde real stakes, real knowledge, and real reasons to be the one doing this, which made me feel like the session was built for this character specifically.

free_text.best_moment: The second attempt at reading the swarm-song's weakness that succeeded — calling out exactly where the hive-touched flinched because thirty years of fisher-reflex ran deeper than the song could override. Aldous's whole concept of reading patterns in drowning things finally landed as a decisive tactical contribution, not just flavor.
free_text.most_frustrating: The first Lore attack on the swarm-song completely whiffed. Thematically it felt right — using his deep knowledge of omens and breaking-points to strike where the song frayed — but mechanically it failed, and no reroll/invoke would have helped. Felt like reaching for something just outside his grasp, which was realistic but unsatisfying in the moment.
free_text.background_used: Good. The Corvus/Bogmere Crossing trauma was woven in as the emotional core of the rushing-vs-caution tension without overshadowing the other players' moments. The compel worked because it was specific and earned — Aldous accepting it after refusing it once created real weight. Rain-reading as his core skill was used consistently across scenes without becoming a crutch.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More decisive agency in the final ford crossing's tactical execution. Ysolde found the hidden channel, Mire knew the stair route, Aldous marked the deep water—but the outcome felt somewhat predetermined by the three characters' collected knowledge rather than Aldous making a choice that altered the situation. Also left the Warden skiff thread hanging; curious what happens when they report this crossing.
free_text.one_sentence: Aldous's backstory felt earned and organic — the rain-reading and Corvus trauma emerged naturally from his concept and skills without being forced or overshadowing others' arcs.

free_text.best_moment: When Morwen's rite broke the swarm-song's hold on Kess at Gullet Ford—proof that her exorcism actually works and her vow against burning has real power to save people.
free_text.most_frustrating: The quiet playstyle naturally means less spotlight than louder characters; not a GM issue, just the nature of playing someone who speaks only when addressed.
free_text.background_used: Good. The vow against burning was directly woven in—helping Yara's daughter without Wardens knowing—and Morwen's exorcist rites were essential to both Kess and Peren's rescues.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted more moments where Morwen was the protagonist of an exorcism scene rather than support—where her specific expertise was the centerpiece of the rescue, not just one tool among others.
free_text.one_sentence: My background was respected and my abilities mattered in key moments, but the narrative spotlight went more to other characters' personal stakes (Ysolde's sister, Mire's temple) than to Morwen's own story.

free_text.best_moment: Grabbing Peren off the bell-frame with a Legendary roll—everything about Mire in one moment: trained from childhood, refusing to break, temple-sworn, determined not to abandon people.
free_text.most_frustrating: First two acts felt like supporting Ysolde's story rather than having Mire's own stakes; the Wardens spotting us crossing without toll should have created more real consequences.
free_text.background_used: Good—the temple orphanage was woven naturally throughout and central to the rescue. The militia training showed up at every conflict. It felt earned, not forced.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More collision between Mire's duties and her real obligations—I expected the Cartel debt and Warden disgrace to create actual complications, not just a clean heroic arc.
free_text.one_sentence: Your temple background made the rescue meaningful and earned, but my past as a disgraced Warden never really caught up with me.

chronicle.summary: Fleeing the drowned ford where Kess's hive-touched pack broke and scattered, the party carried their wounds into Hollowmoot, won Mother Yara's trust, and crossed the rising, Pikemaw-haunted water to Saint Orrin's belltower. There Mire, Ysolde, Aldous, and Morwen tore young Peren free from the Hive Mother's swarm-song and the bell-rope she'd bound him to, leaving her patient breath below the nave thwarted but undrowned. The session closes with the boy alive in Mire's arms, the Wardens now aware of an illegal ford crossing, and the Hive Mother's hunger in the belltower still very much unfinished business.
